param.name: exposure
param.label: Exposure column
param.help: Numeric, TIME-VARYING column in the phenotype table. A time-invariant column cannot be estimated by a within-subject model.

param.name: exposure_scale
param.label: Exposure scale
param.help: The exposure is divided by this, so effects read per unit. 100 gives effect per 100 days.

param.name: subject
param.label: Subject identifier column
param.help: Repeated measures are grouped by this. Subject intercepts absorb array type, cohort and chip when those are nested within subject.

param.name: covars
param.label: Time-varying covariates (comma separated)
param.help: Only time-varying covariates are usable. Age and sex are constant within a subject and are removed exactly by the within transform, so listing them has no effect.

macros.token:
**Why a within-subject model**
In a two-cohort 450K + EPIC study every Sentrix chip is nested inside one array type, so array type is perfectly collinear with cohort and with chip. No design matrix can separate them. What *is* estimable is the within-subject change over the exposure, because each subject sits entirely on one array: the subject intercept absorbs array, cohort and chip together, exactly, and the exposure coefficient is identified from repeated visits of the same person.
